This haiku exemplifies the tension between tradition and existential dread, a hallmark of modern *haiku* that subverts classical expectations. In the broader context of Japanese poetry, this work echoes the *sabi* (寂) of late Bashō or the *wabi* (侘) of Issa, but with a modern, almost nihilistic edge. Where those poets found solace in impermanence, this haiku finds only the mockery of impermanence—the light of spring is not a promise but a taunt.
